focus: CI on/off control part 2: evaluate a committed config, an env file read by a gate job, and workflow_dispatch inputs against the vars.* design; test hook-flags.env and .env.example reuse; assess pull_request_target security; recommend one design with the exact gate-job shape
answeredQuestions: What on/off control design lets a clone or base repo disable workflows or groups without editing YAML?

graphEvents.label: vars.* master switch over five README-tier groups, off as sole disable token
Skipped-job check semantics remains unverified after two 404 fetches

label: workflow_dispatch inputs cannot control push-triggered runs: the inputs context is populated only for a manual dispatch, so inputs.ci != 'off' is TRUE on the 28 push-triggered workflows that spend the runner minutes; a dispatch input is also per-run state and cannot express a standing preference. The repo has never used inputs either - nine workflows declare workflow_dispatch and none declares an inputs block (gate-inputs.yml:6 is followed directly by permissions: at :8).

hook-flags.env cannot be the CI control and the repo says so: hook-flags.env.example:55 states 'CI never reads this file, so the repository's own checks stay on there', and the live file is gitignored (.gitignore:355) and absent from a checkout. The committed .env.example is a comment template - its rows are commented definitions (.env.example:110) and only the section-1 secret placeholders are uncommented and empty (.env.example:58) - so a parser reads comments. Reusable part is the contract only (hook-flags.env.example:5 'Every hook is ON by default', master switch idiom at :17, env-wins precedence at .env.example:275), which vars.* reproduces natively.

A committed config (.skilled/ci.json) is the only rival design that creates attack surface, and pull_request_target is currently absent repo-wide (zero matches across all 33 workflows). A job-level if: cannot read a file, so the config route needs a checkout-and-parse job; reading the base repo's config while evaluating a PR is what pulls in pull_request_target with its write token and secrets. No such config exists today either - .skilled/ holds only package.json, package-lock.json, specs/descriptions.json and specs/graph-metadata.json. The vars.* design needs no job, no checkout and no privileged trigger, so the question never arises.

Recommended switch: SKILLED_CI master over five group keys (TESTS, REPORTS, REVIEW, FRESHNESS, MESSAGES) derived from the README Push-versus-PR tier table at README.md:60, whose guards row (:66) and path-filtered row (:69) already name every member - six variables for 33 workflows, and the list changes only when a README tier changes. 'off' is the sole disable token: vars.X != 'off' runs the job for 0, false, no and typos alike, which is deliberately fail-safe but must be documented because a user will set SKILLED_CI_TESTS=0 and conclude the switch is broken. dependabot-auto-merge gets no switch: safety-relevant, one job, nothing gained.

Exact gate-job shape: 'if: vars.SKILLED_CI != 'off' && vars.SKILLED_CI_<GROUP> != 'off'' inserted between the job's name: and runs-on:, matching the tree's densest gate job (gate-inputs.yml:12-14). No ${{ }} wrapper, because a bare job-level if: is already an expression - which is how the four existing conditions are written (trigger-index-rebuild.yml:33). Where an event condition already exists it must be ANDed and both sides parenthesised, never replaced: replacing trigger-index-rebuild.yml:33's !endsWith loop guard would silently drop it. This is the one scoped edit that can regress behaviour, so it needs its own review rule.

The branch-protection comparison still cannot be made, and it now has two independent failures: GitHub's 'use conditions to control job execution' page returned HTTP 404 again (second attempt; iteration 10 also 404), and the repository records no required-check set anywhere in-tree - rg for 'required status check|branch protection|required check|status check' over .github/workflows/README.md and docs/ returns zero matches. The claim that a skipped job satisfies a required check therefore remains inferred. Mitigation rather than resolution: phase 002 gates only SKILLED_CI_TESTS and SKILLED_CI_REPORTS, leaving the tree-wide freshness guards and the message contract ungateable, so a blocking skipped check strands a suite PR rather than a guard PR.

Clone default-ON is structural (git clone transfers the commit graph, not repository settings, so no vars value travels and every job runs); fork default-ON is inferred (a PR from a fork runs in the base repository's context, so base-repo variables apply and a contributor cannot disable CI from their own fork). The design's asymmetry to document: variable state lives outside the repo and outside code review, unlike the gitignored hook-flags.env whose whole point is being local.

The 'advisory jobs that never gate' half of the overengineering question is partly closed and the hypothesis inverts: the advisory job is deliberate and documented. advisory-checks.yml:16 states 'continue-on-error keeps the job green: a red X nobody is expected to act on is how a gate becomes background noise', with the job at :19-20 and its steps carrying continue-on-error: true; a second instance is strict-pass-freshness-report.yml:165. The open question about these jobs is cost-versus-signal, not whether they should gate. The pre-commit-duplicate half stays open.

direction: Use workflow_dispatch inputs as the on/off control (per-run toggle)
reason: Inputs are populated only for a manual dispatch, so the condition is TRUE on every push- and PR-triggered run - exactly the runs that cost runner minutes; and a per-run input cannot express a standing preference. No workflow in the tree declares an inputs block either.

direction: Reuse .skilled/hooks/hook-flags.env as the CI control file
reason: Gitignored and absent from a checkout, and hook-flags.env.example:55 states CI never reads it. The committed .env.example is a comment template, not a machine-read config.

direction: Introduce a committed .skilled/ci.json read by a gate job
reason: Needs a checkout-and-parse job in every workflow that wants a switch, is the only design that raises a pull_request_target exposure question, and would be the tree's first privileged-trigger workflow - against a switch a single expression already covers.

direction: Put a per-workflow switch on all 33 workflows
reason: 33 variables drift on every workflow addition with no check able to catch the drift; the README tier table already defines six groups and its row is the documented place a new workflow registers.
